title: CHAPTER ELEVEN. On the sacraments in general: definition
latin: CAPUT UNDECIMUM, De sacramentis in genere. Atque haec de VERBO, primo medio externo salutis: sequitur alterum nimirum SACRAMENTUM, quod est actio sacra solennis peculiari Dei verbo instituta, qua cum visibili & externo elemento mystice unita res coelestis & invisibilis dispensatur, ad hominibus offerendam, applicandam & obsignandam Euangelii promissionem. Eademque sermo Graecis mysterion dicitur. Originem nominis posse Hebraicam ait Casaubonus. Sacramenta & mysteria nuncuparunt rerum invisibilium signa visibilia, quae Deus ipse in ecclesia sua instituit.
english: CHAPTER ELEVEN. On the sacraments in general.

Thus far concerning the WORD, the first external means of salvation; there follows the second, namely the SACRAMENT, which is a sacred solemn action instituted by a peculiar word of God, by which a heavenly and invisible thing mystically united with a visible external element is dispensed, for offering, applying, and sealing the Gospel promise to humans. The same speech the Greeks call mystery.
Casaubon holds the name's origin may be Hebrew. They called sacraments and mysteries visible signs of invisible things that God Himself instituted in His church.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Casaubon holds ye name's origin may be Hebrew. They called sacraments and mysteries visible signs belonging toward invisible things that God Himself instituted in His church. — Thus far concerning ye WORD, ye first external means belonging toward salvation; there follows ye second, namely ye SACRAMENT, which stands as a sacred solemn action instituted by a peculiar word belonging toward God, by which a heavenly and invisible thing mystically united with a visible external element stands as dispensed, for offering, applying, and sealing ye Gospel promise toward humans. Ye same speech ye Greeks call mystery. — CHAPTER ELEVEN. On ye sacraments in general.

title: II. Rules for understanding the sacrament definition (1–3)
latin: II. Ad sacramenti definitionem rectius intelligendam observandae sunt hae regulae. 1. Sola divina institutio Sacramentum efficit, qua sublata tollitur & mutata mutatur. IN SUBSTANTIALIBUS SACRAMENTI NIHIL MUTANDUM EST. 2. Etiamsi sacramenta sint signa, tamen non sunt vacua signa, sed rei signatae, gratiae nimirum spiritualis, tanquam ad ea velate exhibitiva. 3. Unio sacramentalis non est essentialis naturalis, sed mystica, non ficta sed vera & realis, coniunctio rei terrenae & caelestis arctissima, qua fit ut in legitimo usu una earum dicta & exhibita una vere etiam secundum formulam promissionis credenti exhibeatur altera.
english: II. These rules help understand the definition. 1. Divine institution alone makes a Sacrament; remove it and the sacrament is removed, change it and it is changed. IN THE SUBSTANTIALS OF A SACRAMENT NOTHING IS TO BE CHANGED.
2. Though sacraments are signs, they are not empty signs, but exhibitve of the thing signified—namely spiritual grace—as veiled under them.

3. Sacramental union is not essential-natural but mystical, not feigned but true and real: the closest conjunction of earthly and heavenly thing, so that in lawful use, when one is named and exhibited, the other is truly exhibited to the believer according to the promise's formula.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 3. Sacramental union stands as not essential-natural but mystical, not feigned but true and real: ye closest conjunction belonging toward earthly and heavenly thing, so that in lawful use, when one stands as named and exhibited, ye other stands as truly exhibited toward ye believer according toward ye promise's formula. — 2. Though sacraments stand as signs, they stand as not empty signs, but exhibitve belonging toward ye thing signified—namely spiritual grace—as veiled under them. — II. These rules help understand ye definition. 1. Divine institution alone makes a Sacrament; remove it and ye sacrament stands as removed, change it and it stands as changed. title: Rules 4–6: instruments of grace; faith; necessity
latin: 4. Sacramenta sunt etiam media sive instrumenta per quae gratia Euangelii non tantum obsignatur & confirmatur, sed etiam vere confertur & applicatur credentibus. Sic Baptismus regenerationi & renovationi Spiritus inseruit (Rom. 6:4); sic per usum s. coenae vita spiritualis reficitur. 5. Deus ipse per sacramenta tanquam instrumenta gratiae virtutem suam exserit ad applicandam & obsignandam gratiam, non quibusvis, sed iis duntaxat qui oblatam vera fide apprehendunt; ac proinde sacramenta gratiam neque physice sibi inhaerentem habent, neque ex opere operato exhibent. Qui sine fide utuntur, non tantum gratiam nullam acquirunt, sed gravissimum onus irae divinae sibi imponunt (1 Cor. 11:27-29). 6. Usus sacramentorum nec arbitrarius nec supervacuus est, sed necessarius ex ordinatione Dei: non ita simpliciter ut praedicatio verbi, sed ita ut in casu necessitatis ea intermitti ad tempus possint. Regula: Non privatio, sed contemptus sacramentorum damnat.
english: 4. Sacraments are also means or instruments through which Gospel grace is not only sealed and confirmed but truly conferred and applied to believers—baptism to regeneration (Rom. 6:4); the Supper to refresh spiritual life.

5. God Himself through the sacraments as instruments of grace exerts His power to apply and seal grace, not to any whatsoever, but only to those who apprehend what is offered by true faith. Sacraments neither have grace physically inhering nor exhibit it ex opere operato. Those who use them without faith acquire no grace and impose on themselves the heaviest burden of divine wrath (1 Cor. 11:27-29).

6. Their use is neither arbitrary nor superfluous but necessary from God's ordinance—not as simply as the preaching of the word, yet so that in a case of necessity they may be interrupted for a time. The rule: Not privation, but contempt of the sacraments damns.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 6. Their use stands as neither arbitrary nor superfluous but necessary from God's ordinance—not as simply as ye preaching belonging toward ye word, yet so that in a case belonging toward necessity they may be interrupted for a time. God Himself through ye sacraments as instruments belonging toward grace exerts His power toward apply and seal grace, not toward any whatsoever, but only toward those who apprehend what stands as offered by true faith. Sacraments neither have grace physically inhering nor exhibit it ex opere operato. Those who use them without faith acquire no grace and impose on themselves ye heaviest burden belonging toward divine wrath (1 Cor. 11:27-29). — 4. Sacraments stand as also means or instruments through which Gospel grace stands as not only sealed and confirmed but truly conferred and applied toward believers—baptism toward regeneration (Rom. 6:4); ye Supper toward refresh spiritual life.

title: III. Sacraments of Old and New Testament; Cap.12 next
latin: III. Sunt autem sacramenta alia veteris, alia Novi Testamenti. Ante Abrahamum Ecclesia fuit sine sacramentis stricte sumptis, solo verbo pasta; etiamsi in statu integritatis arbor vitae quadam sacramentali significatione Christum ostenderit, & post lapsum signa sacramentalia extraordinaria fuerunt (arca Noae, 1 Pet. 3:20-21; 1 Cor. 10:1-4). CAPUT DUODECIMUM sequitur, De sacramentis veteris testamenti.
english: III. There are sacraments of the Old Testament and of the New. Before Abraham the Church was without sacraments strictly so called, fed by the word alone—though in integrity the tree of life showed Christ with a kind of sacramental signification, and after the fall there were extraordinary sacramental signs (Noah's ark, 1 Pet. 3:20-21; 1 Cor. 10:1-4).
CHAPTER TWELVE follows, On the sacraments of the Old Testament.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWELVE follows, On ye sacraments belonging toward ye Old Testament. — III. There stand as sacraments belonging toward ye Old Testament and belonging toward ye New.
